$comment: The registry of generated-and-committed artifacts: what each is generated from, the command that regenerates it, the gate that judges it, and whether a commit is checked against it.

WHY. A generated file goes stale whenever one of its inputs is committed without it. Three times on 2026-10-13 that was found late: 8dbb6066e left the CLI contract stale for 40 minutes; agent/plans/QUEUE.md was regenerated in the working tree and never committed, and PR 600 run 38381096702 went red on it; a new test file needed gen-docs --write, which the gen-docs pre-commit check caught at the commit. The third is the model, and this file extends it.

READ BY .claude/rediacc_hooks/git/artifacts.py (the git-level pre-commit hook, from the COMMIT'S index) and judged by .ci/scripts/quality/check_generated_artifacts.py (check:ci-generated-artifacts): an input or output glob that matches no tracked file, a generator or gate that does not exist, an enrolled entry without a check, a budget or a control, and an entry left out of the commit-time check without a reason are each a finding.

`when`: `commit` runs `commit.check` in a scratch checkout of the commit's index whenever the commit changes a path matching `inputs` (minus `inputs_exclude`) or `outputs`, and refuses the commit when it exits `commit.stale_exit` (default 1); any other non-zero exit, a missing `commit.requires` path and a run longer than `commit.budget_s` are refused as UNCHECKED. `commit-dedicated` is checked at commit time by its own code path, named in `reason`. `pre-push` is left to its gate in the pre-push run and CI, with the reason.

`commit.links` are untracked build products of the working tree linked into the scratch tree (a link the working tree lacks is skipped); `commit.requires` must exist in the working tree, each with the command that creates it; `commit.env_remove` are environment variables the checker must not inherit. `commit.blind` says what the commit-time run cannot see and the gate can.

`commit.control` is the planted defect .claude/rediacc_hooks/tests/test_githook_generated_artifacts.py commits through the real hook: `replace` rewrites `old` to `new` in an input, `create` adds a new input file. The commit must be refused naming `generator`, the same commit with the regenerated outputs must pass, and a commit of an unrelated path must not run the checker.

`measured_s` is the gate's wall time on 2026-10-13 on the development machine, the number the commit-or-pre-push decision was made from. TO ENROL an artifact: give its gate a mode that needs no network and no history beyond the tree, measure it, declare the inputs and a control, and run the test file.

commit.blind: The generator imports @rediacc/shared and @rediacc/provisioning through their built dist in the working tree, so a staged change under packages/shared/src outside cli-contract/ is judged only as far as that build is current. check:ci-cli-contract builds first and is the verdict before a push.
Only R8, RQ and RQ-SETTINGS run (the two rendered files against their renders). R1 to R7, R9, RB and the census need history and the full gate's 77 s, and stay in the pre-push run.

control.content:
# PLAN: the generated-artifacts control

Status: approved

## Tasks

- [ ] T1 a box the queue must list

commit.blind: The lock's own selftest does not run at commit time; check:ci-gates-lock runs it.

artifacts.title: Generated doc regions
artifacts.reason: Checked at commit time by `gen_docs_pre_commit` in .claude/rediacc_hooks/git/githooks.py, which predates this registry and asks the generator itself (`--affected`) which staged paths are inputs: each provider declares its own `inputs` in scripts/lib/doc-providers.ts, so the two globs here name only the machinery and the full input set is not repeated.

artifacts.title: CLI command tree
artifacts.reason: It has the CLI contract's inputs and a second exporter run of its own, so enrolling it doubles what every CLI commit pays, and its gate has no no-build mode yet. The next candidate: add the mode, measure, enrol.

artifacts.title: Plan box ledger
artifacts.reason: Its verdict includes A1, a box that vanished since the base ref, which reads history the scratch tree is not set up to prove. Cheap enough to enrol once it has a tree-only mode.

artifacts.title: Translation hash manifests
artifacts.reason: Deterministic and cheap, and deliberately not a commit-time fix: regenerating the hashes is the LOCK step that follows re-translating the changed keys, so a refusal that printed the generator would invite locking stale translations. The gate's own message gives the order. It also reads the private/account submodule, which a scratch checkout of the index does not hold.

artifacts.title: Derived locale files
artifacts.reason: NOT deterministic and never run automatically: `i18n:sync` rewrote 12 locales on a clean tree. The locales are naturalized by hand and by the pipeline in docs/i18n/CONVENTIONS.md; the generator is named here so that nobody enrols it.

artifacts.title: Shard manifests
artifacts.reason: Its real inputs are every test file of six lanes, three of them inside the private/renet and private/account submodules (one enumerated by `go list`), which a scratch checkout of the index does not hold; the three globs name only the machinery. 6.8 s on every commit that adds a test is also above what a commit should pay.

artifacts.title: Python environment registry
artifacts.reason: 24.7 s, and every tracked Python module is an input, so most commits would pay it. It is also shrink-only: a new environment read is reviewed, not regenerated away.

artifacts.title: Hook inventory and coverage baselines
artifacts.generator: hand-edited: drain the one line the gate names
artifacts.reason: A baseline, not a render: removing a guard is a deliberate act and the baseline is drained by hand in the same commit, so there is no generator a refusal could print.

artifacts.title: Inline suppression baseline
artifacts.reason: Shrink-only: `--write-baseline` records a drain and refuses growth, and a new suppression is fixed, never baselined, so the command must not be offered as the fix for a refused commit. Its inputs are every source file in the tree; the glob names only the gate.

artifacts.title: Workflow steps bound from gate headers
artifacts.reason: 6.1 s with every gate source as an input, so most CI commits would pay it; check:ci-parity and check:ci-gate-bind judge it in the pre-push run.
